title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This handwritten page is written on the back of a typed page of SGA 7, exposé IX (Néron models, toric part, the dual graph of a curve). It sets up the framework in which the notes treat the cohomology of simplicial sets.

1. Let (SS) = Δ^ = Hom(Δ^op, Ens) be the category of semi-simplicial (simplicial) sets. It is a presheaf topos.
2. For a simplicial set X, the slice (SS)/X is again a topos, the 'induced topos'. It is canonically equivalent to the presheaf topos on the category of simplices: (SS)/X ≃ (Δ/X)^ = Hom((Δ/X)^op, Ens). This is the standard equivalence 'slice of presheaves = presheaves on the category of elements'.
3. Grothendieck declares that, for his purposes, the cohomological study of X is the study of this induced topos.
4. So the sheaves 'on X' are the simplicial sets F → X over X, equivalently functors (Δ/X)^op → Ens. Abelian sheaves are abelian group objects over X, equivalently functors (Δ/X)^op → Ab. The same holds for sheaves of differential graded rings, etc.
5. For a simplicial set A, the projection A×X → X is a sheaf on X. It is the pullback A_X of A along the localisation morphism (SS)/X → (SS), and also the composite functor (Δ/X)^op → Δ^op → Ens (the second arrow being A).

Purpose in the manuscript (the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex): this provides a topos-theoretic home for sheaves of DG algebras on a simplicial set X. Examples are a 'simplicial de Rham complex' with divided powers (an integral analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms) and constant coefficients A_X. The cohomology of X with coefficients is then computed in the topos (Δ/X)^. For constant coefficients this agrees with ordinary simplicial cohomology, because the nerve of Δ/X is weakly equivalent to X.
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalence (SS)/X ≃ presheaves on Δ/X and the description of constant sheaves are correct.

Implicit point: general (non-locally-constant) presheaves on Δ/X have cohomology that need not be invariant under weak equivalence of X. Only locally constant coefficients give homotopy-invariant cohomology. The page does not discuss this.

ideas.what: The slice topos of simplicial sets over X is equivalent to presheaves on the category of simplices Δ/X
ideas.modern_name: category of elements / slice of presheaf topos; category of simplices
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 exp. III-IV (induced topos); the theme also recurs in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Defining the cohomology of a simplicial set X as the cohomology of the topos (Δ/X)^, with sheaves of abelian groups and of DG rings as functors on (Δ/X)^op
ideas.modern_name: cohomology of simplicial sets via the presheaf topos on the category of simplices; coefficient systems on simplicial sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Gabriel–Zisman; Illusie's Complexe cotangent; later Moerdijk)

ideas.what: Constant sheaf A_X as A×X → X, i.e. the composite (Δ/X)^op → Δ^op → Ens
ideas.modern_name: pullback of a constant presheaf along the localisation morphism

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard topos-theoretic preliminary material (slice topos = presheaves on the category of simplices). Its only interest is that it shows how Grothendieck framed the simplicial divided-power de Rham complex: as sheaves of DG algebras on the topos (Δ/X)^. That framing is natural and already implicit in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Les faisceaux (donc) [-sur-] X" sont...': the manuscript reads roughly 'Les faisceaux "sur X" sont les faisceaux semi-simpliciaux F → X sur X'. The inserted word is '(donc)' above 'sur'; 'sur' is not clearly struck.
The last line seems to read '(Δ/X)° → (Δ)° → (Ens)' with A over the arrow; the transcription is essentially right.
